summary: Discusses why the IP6.ARPA DNS zone needs delegation and specifies a plan for operating it. It was replaced by RFC 3596.

plainLanguage.summary: It sets up the lookup directory that turns the new long addresses back into names.

subtitle: Why IPv6 reverse lookups moved from IP6.INT to IP6.ARPA, and who runs the new zone.

tldr.problem: IPv6 needed reverse mapping of addresses to DNS names, like IN-ADDR.ARPA provides for IPv4, and earlier documents pointed to IP6.INT.
tldr.mechanism: It deprecates IP6.INT in five earlier RFCs and asks IANA to delegate IP6.ARPA, with names further delegated to the regional IP registries following address space assignment.
tldr.outcome: It was obsoleted by RFC 3596, so it is no longer the current statement of IPv6 reverse mapping.

today: RFC 3152 is a Best Current Practice (BCP 49) that was obsoleted by RFC 3596, so it is no longer the current definition. It updated RFC 1886, RFC 2553, RFC 2766, RFC 2772 and RFC 2874.

sections.title: Why IP6.ARPA
sections.content:
In the IPv6 address space there is a need for reverse mapping of addresses to DNS names, analogous to what the IN-ADDR.ARPA zone provides for IPv4.

The IAB recommended that the ARPA top level domain be used for technical infrastructure sub-domains when possible. The name is now considered an acronym for 'Address and Routing Parameters Area'. ARPA is already used for IPv4 reverse mapping and for E.164 numbering on the Internet. IETF consensus was reached that IP6.ARPA be used for address to DNS name mapping for IPv6, as noted in RFC 2874.
sections.plainLanguage: Phone books let you find a name from a number. IPv6 needed its own number-to-name book, and it was put in the same place as the other ones.

sections.title: Deprecating IP6.INT
sections.content:
The document deprecates references to IP6.INT in RFC 1886 (section 2.5), RFC 2553 (section 6.2.3), RFC 2766 (section 4.1), RFC 2772 (section 7.1.c) and RFC 2874 (section 2.5). That is why it is marked as updating those RFCs.

'Deprecate' here means the old usage is not appropriate for new implementations, and IP6.INT will likely be phased out in an orderly fashion.
sections.plainLanguage: An old street name is being retired. New maps should use the new name, while the old one fades out slowly.

sections.title: Delegation and Security
sections.content:
The memo requests that IANA delegate the IP6.ARPA domain following instructions to be provided by the IAB. Names within the zone are to be further delegated to the regional IP registries in accordance with the delegation of IPv6 address space to those registries. The names allocated should be hierarchic in accordance with the address space assignment.

On security, the RFC notes that DNS spoofing of address to name mapping has been exploited in IPv4, but says delegating IP6.ARPA creates no new threats to the security of the internet.
sections.plainLanguage: The big directory is handed to the groups that hand out addresses, and each one looks after its own pages.
